meta.title: Pashto Quest — Week 2 Content Bank
meta.inherits: Existing 4-zone game and Week 1 navigation, player progress and XP rules. No new interaction modes.
meta.scope: CONTENT IMPLEMENTATION PACKAGE, not yet installed in the playable game
meta.language_policy: English intentions are canonical content; Pashto models are provisional and require a Laghman native speaker review before release; no automated synthesized audio is falsely labelled native.
meta.daily_skip_rule: Day 8+ challenges selectable immediately, skip does not mark visits complete. Day 8 accessible only once Day 7 weekly exam passed in final integration.
meta.week2_levels: TBD; do not change Week 1 Level 10 graduation or add XP assumptions

days.title: This One or That One?
days.intro: Saleha points to a book beside the player, a bird farther along the water, and two baskets at different distances. She explains that Pashto دا and هغه can point to things; هغه also occurs as he/she, so the surrounding noun and conversational context matter. Use دغه as an optional familiar local near form only after review.
grammar: A demonstrative identifies which noun is meant, not who performs an action.
Pashto دا can modify a singular or plural noun; unlike English, it does not automatically change from this to these.
The demonstrative هغه and the he/she pronoun share a spelling; distinguish meaning by structure and stress (pronunciation audit).
Keep gender/number agreement on adjectives and equatives.
models: This book is new. (near alternative; native review)

Lake · Saleha: That bird is near the tree.
This stone is beside the water.

days.challenge: Saleha describes nearby and distant objects at the lakeside; player identifies intended objects and constructs demonstrative sentences.
assessment: Choose this/that from given relative distance
Sentence construction with demonstrative + noun + adjective

days.title: One, Two, Many
days.topic: Plural nouns, agreement and small quantities
days.intro: Edris receives a delivery and asks the player to sort individual items and groups. Singular and plural words are heard in meaningful sentences. Numbers one to five are introduced for simple counts.
new: یو / دوه / درې / څلور / پنځه — one to five
grammar: Pluralisation is noun-class dependent; ـونه works with many inanimate consonant-ending masculine nouns, while many ـه feminine nouns form ـې plurals.
Plural adjective/equative agreement must be taught with full examples; avoid guessing based on English endings.
دا can introduce both singular and plural noun phrases; the noun and predicate distinguish this/these.
Numerals and counted nouns may involve special agreement/inflection; begin with simple naming/counting tasks and speaker-reviewed sentences.

School · Ms Hameed: There are three students in the classroom.

days.challenge: Edris takes inventory; match quantities to item groups, interpret singular/plural, and assemble agreement-safe sentences.

days.title: Where Is Mina’s Notebook?
days.intro: Mina misplaces a notebook she was using beside the lake. Without adding a new playable map location, the player follows descriptions and speaks to villagers to work out where she left it.
new: تر څنګ — beside (practice as a full phrase)
grammar: Location questions with چېرته often keep ordinary Pashto verb placement.
Pashto commonly uses paired adpositions (e.g. په ... کې) rather than treating every English preposition as one Pashto word.
Keep the difference between a location statement and a movement-to-location sentence; school ته ځي is movement.
Do not introduce the full case-inflection system yet; teach fixed common phrases and mark inflection-sensitive forms for review.

Lake · Mina and Saleha: The fish is in the river.
School · Ms Hameed: The book is on the table.
The notebook is in the classroom.
Market · Edris: The apples are in the basket.
The grocer is at the shop.
Home · Muhammad Jan: The chair is beside the door.
The book is on the table.
The book is in this room.

days.challenge: Mina retraces her route. Questions describe locations; the player interprets clues to identify the notebook’s location through dialogue only.

days.title: Whose Things Are These?
days.intro: Muhammad Jan finds household belongings mixed with items belonging to Mina and Saleha. He asks the player to identify the owner of each, building on this/that and plurals.
new: ستاسو / ستاسې — your (polite/plural; check local preference)
د هغه / د هغې — his / her (case and referent sensitive)
grammar: Possession often uses a possessor before the noun: زما کتاب.
Named possessors can use د + possessor, with gender/case-sensitive forms when applicable.
Pashto possessives are not identical to English apostrophe-s; teach whole natural phrases.
Distinguish pronoun person from owner rather than allowing ambiguous his/her questions.

School · Ms Hameed: Your notebook is on the table.

days.challenge: Muhammad Jan sorts misplaced possessions after a visit; the player identifies owners in an everyday conversation.
assessment: Recall noun plurals in possessive phrases

days.title: Ask the Right Question
days.topic: Who, what, which, where, how many
days.intro: Ms Hameed runs a classroom investigation. The player learns to ask purposeful questions rather than merely answering prompts: identify people, objects, choices, places and quantities.
grammar: Pashto question words generally appear in the position corresponding to the information requested rather than forcing English word order.
Yes/no questions can use rising intonation; wh-questions use interrogative words.
Some question words and adjectives change form with gender/case; only teach verified examples initially.
A question must be pragmatically natural with a sensible answer; do not test arbitrary grammar strings.

Market · Edris: How many apples do you buy?
Lake · Saleha and Mina: Who is running beside the lake?
Which bird is near the water?
How many fish do we see?

days.challenge: A short classroom interview led by Ms Hameed; select suitable questions and respond using familiar vocabulary.
assessment: Choose sensible question word for an answer
Distinguish where from which and whose

days.title: How We Do Things
days.topic: Adverbs: time, manner, frequency and group action
days.intro: Saleha and Mina compare everyday routines. One walks slowly, another runs quickly, and everyone describes what they normally do at different places.
new: سبا — tomorrow (time word only; do not teach future tense yet)
grammar: Adverbs add information about how, when, or how often an action occurs.
Do not teach “tomorrow” as a future tense form: restrict practice to timetable phrases or leave it receptive.
Adverbs and adverbial phrases may vary in position; accept contextually natural variants supported by the language reviewer.
Reuse known present-tense verbs so the new challenge is the adverb, not a new conjugation.
models: I am reading a book today.

Lake · Saleha and Mina: They sometimes sit beside the lake.
Market · Edris: Edris opens his shop every day.

days.challenge: Saleha and Mina plan a routine walk around town; identify how/when actions take place and form meaningful sentences with adverbs.
assessment: Add manner to an existing sentence
Add time/frequency without changing present tense
Revisit group pronouns and plural nouns

days.title: The Village Scavenger Hunt
days.topic: Integrated Week 2 revision; no new core grammar
days.intro: Muhammad Jan sets the player a series of clues involving all four village locations; Ms Hameed administers an extended Week 2 assessment. Scavenger-hunt stops use existing dialogue/lesson cards, not object-moving or a new explorable region.
grammar: No new grammar: use the week’s topics in combined, meaningful contexts.
Interpret each clue before forming a sentence.
Require nouns and verbs that match everyday scenes.
Correctly recognise speaker, intended addressee and referenced object.
models: موږ یو ځای ښوونځي ته ځو.

Home · Muhammad Jan: Your book is on that chair.
Lake · Saleha and Mina: Those birds are near the river.

days.challenge: Week 2 culminating challenge: Ms Hameed reviews 25 contextual prompts framed as village scavenger-hunt clues (20/25 to pass), with cumulative Week 1 integration.
assessment: 5 integrated sentence construction, mixed pronouns and speaker/addressee
